Help.Title: VoiceType — Help
Help.Start.Title: Getting started
Help.Start.Body:
1. On first start the recommended speech model downloads automatically.
2. Tap the round **Record** button at the bottom and speak — the transcript appears live. Recording continues until you tap the button again; there is no need to hold it.
3. Open the menu **≡** (top left) to switch modes — **Inject text** types each final phrase into the focused window, **Live translation** adds a translation card, **Manual input** lets you type or edit the transcript.
4. The menu also holds the recognition language, speech models, downloads and **Settings**— the line under the title shows the active model and modes.
Help.Hotkey.Title: Global hotkey
Help.Hotkey.Body: The default toggle hotkey is **Ctrl+Shift+V**. On Linux it is registered through the XDG GlobalShortcuts portal (xdg-desktop-portal ≥ 1.18, GNOME 44+ / KDE Plasma 5.27+); the compositor shows a one-time consent dialog. On desktops without portal support the hotkey is reported as unavailable.
Help.LinuxInjection.Title: Text injection on Linux
Help.LinuxInjection.Body:
Injection sets the clipboard, then synthesizes the paste chord (Ctrl+V by default — configurable in Settings) into the focused window.

**Required tools (install one per pair):**
• Clipboard: wl-copy (Wayland) or xclip / xsel (X11)
• Keyboard: ydotool (Wayland, needs ydotoold) or libXtst / xdotool (X11)

Ubuntu: *sudo apt install wl-clipboard xclip xdotool*
Help.Audio.Title: Audio capture
Help.Audio.Body:
Capture goes through the PulseAudio-compatible server (PipeWire desktop setups and WSLg both provide one).
• Mic — default input source
• Loopback — monitor of the default output (*@DEFAULT_MONITOR@*)
• Mix — both, merged 50/50
Help.Data.Title: Data locations
Help.Data.Body:
• Settings: *~/.local/share/VoiceType/settings.json*
• Models: *~/.local/share/VoiceType/models/*
(on Windows these resolve under %LOCALAPPDATA%\VoiceType)
